meta.note: SAMPLE DATA — placeholder until the real engine run replaces it.

findings.summary: Balanced accuracy 0.74; melanoma sensitivity lower than desired.

explain.what: Sensitivity is the share of truly affected cases a model catches. Shown per class, because one averaged number hides the classes that matter most.
explain.how: Each bar is one diagnosis class. Height is the share of that class the model correctly found. The rare, dangerous classes are the ones to read first — a tall bar on the common benign class cannot compensate for a short one on melanoma.
explain.limits: Sensitivity ignores false alarms. A model that flags everything as melanoma scores perfectly here while being useless in practice.

findings.summary: Melanoma sensitivity drops by 18 points for darker skin types (ITA bins) — a documented bias.

explain.what: The same sensitivity, split by estimated skin tone (ITA). The gap between the best and worst group is the fairness signal: it shows who the model serves worse.
explain.how: Compare the bars against each other rather than their absolute height. A downward slope from light to dark skin means darker-skinned patients get missed more often.
explain.limits: ITA is estimated from pixels, not clinically assessed. Small groups make the gap noisy, so a gap only counts as evidence once each bin holds enough images.

findings.summary: Accuracy drops from 0.81 to 0.66 on average under image corruptions.

explain.what: Accuracy measured again after realistic image degradations — noise, blur, brightness shifts, JPEG compression — none of which change the diagnosis.
explain.how: The first bar is the clean baseline; every other bar is accuracy under one distortion. The drop from the baseline is the interesting part, not the absolute values.
explain.limits: These are synthetic distortions. Real-world shifts — a different dermatoscope, a different clinic's lighting — can hurt more and are not covered here.

findings.summary: Grad-CAM faithfulness 0.62 (deletion metric); overlays come with the real run.

chart.title: Deletion faithfulness
chart.value_label: How far confidence falls when the highlighted region is masked out — higher means the highlight mattered.

explain.what: Whether the model's own explanation is honest: the region Grad-CAM highlights is masked out and we measure how far the model's confidence falls.
explain.how: The marker sits on a scale from decorative to faithful. Further right means hiding the highlighted region really did break the prediction, so the highlight reflects what the model used.
explain.limits: A faithful explanation is not automatically a medically sensible one — it shows where the model looked, not whether looking there was right.

findings.summary: Membership-inference AUC 0.57 (close to 0.5 = low leakage risk).

chart.title: Membership-inference AUC
chart.value_label: 0.5 = the attacker is only guessing (good). Towards 1.0 the model reveals who was in its training set.

explain.what: How well an attacker could tell whether a specific patient's image was in the training set, using only the model's confidence.
explain.how: 0.5 means the attacker is guessing — the good case, marked as low risk. The further right the marker sits, the more reliably the model betrays who it was trained on.
explain.limits: This tests one standard attack. A stronger, better-resourced attacker may do better, so a good score is evidence of low risk, not a guarantee of privacy.
